processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: All alloys were processed by vacuum induction melting.
The melts were cast into cylindrical copper moulds (32 mm in diameter by 186 mm in length); no further heat treatment reported for the as-cast state.

processing_steps.method: spark erosion cutting and surface grinding (specimen preparation)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Specimens were cut from cast ingots by spark erosion in the direction of the longitudinal axis of the ingot (casting direction); surfaces were ground. Compression samples (6x6x10) mm^3; tensile samples flat (3.5x5) mm^2 cross-section with 15 mm gauge length.

structures.overall_structure: Fe3Al matrix with cube-like TiC precipitates

defect_interactions.interaction_type: intergranular decohesion associated with cube-like TiC precipitates
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Cube-like TiC precipitates can be clearly distinguished on the intergranular fracture areas; the alloy fractured almost completely with intergranular decohesion.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Fe-26Al-based matrix undergoes D0_3/B2 transition at around 550 °C and B2/A2 transition at around 800 °C before melting.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression samples (6x6x10) mm^3; tensile samples flat (3.5x5) mm^2 cross-section with 15 mm gauge length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: ZWICK 1474 universal testing machine; samples cut along casting direction and surfaces ground

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Room-temperature compression stress-strain curve is curve 8 in Fig. 2(b); room-temperature tension curve is curve 8 in Fig. 3(b) (fails below the 300 MPa gridline).

measurement_conditions.temperature: tests up to 800 °C; yield-stress-anomaly peak at about 550 °C
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: radiation furnace; samples held 30 min at testing temperature before loading; NiCr-Ni thermocouple on specimen surface

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 6(a) curve for Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C shows anomalous yield-stress increase with peak near 500-560 °C.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: room-temperature yield stress in compression and matrix hardness

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: load 62.5 g, indentation ball 2.5 mm diameter
characterization_methods.key_findings: Matrix hardness of Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C is 229 HB.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: deformation rate 10^-4 s^-1; elevated-temperature tests in protective argon atmosphere within a radiation furnace; samples held 30 min at testing temperature; NiCr-Ni thermocouple on specimen surface
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine yield stress, stress-strain behaviour and ductility
characterization_methods.key_findings: Room-temperature compression yield stress 454 MPa; yield-stress-anomaly peak at about 550 °C with about 400 MPa; brittle behaviour at room temperature.

characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of fracture surfaces
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM-Hitachi S-530 with 20 kV, working distance 15 mm, secondary electrons (SE)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: fracture surfaces of tensile specimens after room-temperature testing
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C fracture surface is almost entirely smooth intergranular decohesion with scattered cube-like TiC precipitates; fracture mode IGD+TGC; totally brittle behaviour.

unmapped_findings: Fracture mode of Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C after room-temperature tensile testing is IGD+TGC (intergranular decohesion + transgranular cleavage); the alloy fractured almost completely with intergranular decohesion and shows totally brittle behaviour at room temperature (b0033, b0035, figure_004).

In Table 2, yield stress in tension and total elongation for Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C are reported as '-' (not measured/not reported); only matrix hardness (229 HB) and yield stress in compression (454 MPa) are given (b0033).

Ti additions soften Fe-26Al-based alloys: Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C has lower matrix hardness (229 HB vs 260 HB) and lower compression yield stress (454 MPa vs 644 MPa) than binary Fe-26Al (b0021, b0024, b0033).

Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C was tested in tension and compression at 650 °C and 800 °C (Figs. 7 and 8); tension-compression asymmetry is confirmed for all investigated alloys at both temperatures, but no numeric value labels are printed for this alloy in the bar charts (b0040, figure_007, figure_008).
Fe-26Al-based alloys undergo two order-disorder structural transitions: D0_3/B2 at around 550 °C and B2/A2 at around 800 °C before melting (b0012).

At room temperature in compression (Fig. 2b, curve 8), Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C exhibits very high strengthening with almost constant hardening rate until a final parabolic stage of work hardening (b0027, figure_002).
At room temperature in tension (Fig. 3b, curve 8), the Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C curve fails below the 300 MPa gridline, indicating very poor ductility (figure_003).
